comments.value:
What you are experiencing are the limits of the ONSP to SteamAudio conversion code. At a "Max Distance" setting of over approximately 100-200 meters, the math simply doesn't allow for a clean, 1:1 conversion under all circumstances. All design decisions we have made in that algorithm, including the boosted volume for _very_ large distance like your 5000m source, are trade-offs - without them, other worlds would sound incorrect again. There is nothing wrong with using custom audio curves in that scenario, and it is the currently recommended way of approaching it.

The proper fix for this is to provide SteamAudio in the SDK, which is a longer term project we are working towards. Note that this will _not_ allow the mapping to behave like ONSP again, in fact quite the opposite, but it will allow you to use SteamAudio's actual physics based falloffs properly.

Having looked at your world, I don't see anything actionable at the moment that wouldn't break other worlds. Thank your for the detailed bug report either way.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name} Thanks for this fast answer. Does that mean that when I switch globally to custom rolloff in my projects, this option will also stay in future when SteamAudio is added in the SDK? I'd like to avoid having to adjust all my sounds again.
@{5f2eaed841e042066f65cb45|full_name}: Manually configured falloff curves generally sound the same between ONSP and Steam Audio from my experience, so that should be fine.

details:
Compared to the editor, sounds are too loud or too low in the live client.

Steps to reproduce:

- Add 6 audio sources in an empty project and add 6 buttons at spawn to play them individually.

- Place 2 audio sources at 1m distance from spawn. One with far value 500, the other with 5000.

- Repeat that for 5m

- Repeat that for 100m

- Start and stay at the spawn position and push the play buttons one by one.

Play in editor (ONSP):

- The audio sources at 5 m sounds quieter as the audio sources at 1m.

- The audio sources at 100 m sounds quieter as the audio sources at 5m.

- The both audio sources at 1m (one with far value 500 and the other with 5000) has the same level. A difference is noticeable at 5m or even more at 100m.

Play in live client (Steam Audio):

- The audio sources with far value 500 has the same level at 1m and 5m. The level at 1m is too low compared to ONSP.

- The audio sources with far value 5000 is too loud at all level. The level is too high compared to ONSP (overdrives at 1m/5m).

- The both audio sources at 1m (one with far value 500 and the other with 5000) has a completely different level.

- Most audio sources has not the same level compared to ONSP (not even close).

Expected behavior:

- The sounds has a credible and physically correct rolloff.

- At 1m, there is no (big) difference between far 500 and 5000.

- Ideally, the rolloff is the same compared to ONSP, so that world creators has not to re-adjust their 489 audio sources.

Currently its not possible to do a sound design without permanantly uploading and testing live. Also, the rolloff in the client is weird, not logic, simply phyiscally wrong. If we do an adjustment, we will probably have to do it again in future.

I have a demo world (can't make it public right now):

wrld_dc3c7bcf-007a-4286-9561-a8baba69aeec

- The audio sources playing in the 1st row sounds correct in the editor, wrong in the live client.

- The buttons in the 2nd row plays Unity native audio sources (checked "Use Audio Source Volume Curve" in the Spatial Audio Source). Of course, 5000m doesn't make sense there, since Unity always uses a fixed logarithmic rolloff. But it is a good reference, what I would expect at 1m.

- The buttons in the 3rd row plays Unity native audio sources (checked "Use Audio Source Volume Curve" in the Spatial Audio Source, plus a custom script to create a inverse quared rolloff curve similar to editor/ONSP).
title: Volume rolloff in client completely wrong
